::: {#sol-proposition}

- "Add 5 to both sides" is an instruction, so it is neither true nor false.
- "$42$" is a number, not a sentence, so it is neither true nor false.
- "$42$ is an integer" is true.
- "Adding 5 to both sides of $x - 5 = 37$ gives $x = 42$" is true.
- "What is the solution of $2x = 84$?" is a question, so it is neither true nor false.
- "The solution of $2x = 84$ is $41$" is false, since the solution is $42$.
  A false sentence still has a definite truth value.
- "$42$ is not a number" is false.
- "$x$ is a multiple of $8$" is neither until we know $x$:
  it is true when $x = 16$ and false when $x = 3$.

The four sentences with a definite truth value are propositions.
The last sentence, whose truth value depends on $x$, is a predicate.

:::
